title: Influence bound from variance and total influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. Assume $\operatorname{Var}(f)>0$, and set $I=I[f]/\operatorname{Var}(f)$, where $I[f]$ is the sum of the coordinate influences. Then $\frac{9}{I^2}9^{-I}\le M(f)$, where $M(f)$ is the supremum of the absolute coordinate influences (with the empty supremum interpreted as $0$).
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube with variance $V>0$, and put $a=I(f)/V$. Then $(9/a^2)9^{-a}\le\max_{i\in[n]}|I_i(f)|$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
